approval.cost: None stated for API access (API usage is part of the user's Insightly subscription; rate limits are plan-based)
approval.trigger: No review, no approval, no app registration, and no marketplace listing for API access exist in the official documentation. Nothing describes any Insightly-side approval before a third party can call the API with a user's key, and no pre-approval user/install caps exist (each user independently holds a key).

blockers.detail: There is no app registration, no client ID/secret, no authorize endpoint, no consent screen, and no scopes. Insightly's official help article states the API 'expects an Authorization header in HTTPS requests' and 'You will need an API key for each user to uniquely identify them. We use basic authentication'. Onboarding is 'go find a long-lived, full-power credential in your settings and paste it into our app', and the key inherits the user's full access because there are no scopes to narrow it. Insightly's help center mentions OAuth only for Insightly CONSUMING Google/Microsoft OAuth for its own sync features, never for offering OAuth to developers.
blockers.howToClear: No OAuth clearance exists. Design the key-paste flow carefully (secure storage, per-pod URLs, 401 detection) and be transparent about the key's power.
blockers.title: The whole OAuth-shaped hole is the blocker

tested: Read-only verification: the API-key authentication model and the absence of any OAuth/app program were checked against Insightly's official help center, including a search that surfaced 'OAuth' only in connection with Insightly consuming Google/Microsoft OAuth for its own sync features. The complete API reference Insightly names (api.insightly.com/v3.1/Help) documents Basic API-key auth as the mechanism. No account used, nothing submitted.
unverified: Numeric API rate limits per plan (the official article confirms plan-based daily limits and the X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining headers but does not publish the numbers).
Whether Insightly operates any separate partner/integration program outside the API/help documentation (none is referenced in the official API or help pages searched/read).
API key format/length and whether multiple keys per user are possible (the docs describe a single key per user; not stated explicitly).

flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists. The only documented connection: each user pastes their personal API key and API URL (pod) into your product
flavor.why: There is no OAuth app object. The credential is a per-user API key found under User Settings (the API section shows the user's API key and API URL, e.g. https://api.na1.insightly.com; the host varies by 'pod'). Your product calls https://api.{pod}.insightly.com/v3.1/... with Authorization: Basic <Base64(api_key + ':')> (key as username, blank password). Calls act as that user, with that user's permissions and record visibility. No service-account key distinct from a user key is documented either.

humanMust: Each end user opens User Settings in their own Insightly account and copies their API key and API URL/pod (cannot be automated or delegated)
The user pastes both into your product's connect form
The customer's admin must have API Access turned on for the user ('administrators have the ability to turn API Access on or off for any user')
On key reset, the user must paste the new key (your integration fails with 401 until they do)
name: Insightly
nuances: Silent breakage on reset: generating a new key, or changing the user's admin permissions, resets the key. 'Once a new API key has been generated, users must update any applications with the new key in order for them to maintain access to Insightly data.'
The API key does not expire on a schedule; it stays valid until the user generates a new key or their admin permissions change.

Per-user, per-pod sprawl: keys are per user (not per organization) and the base URL depends on the user's pod, so you must store both key and API URL per connection. An admin can turn API Access off for a user at any time, breaking the connection with no documented notice mechanism.
Every API response returns X-RateLimit-Limit (the per-day limit based on plan/subscription) and X-RateLimit-Remaining for the 24-hour period.

API-usage trap from the official docs: when updating an object you must PUT the entire object graph; omitted sub-elements 'will interpret this as a request to remove these sub-elements, a common source of misunderstanding and data loss'.

tagline: Insightly has no OAuth program for third-party apps at all: no app registration, no consent screen, no scopes. The only documented connection is each user pasting their personal API key (and their pod URL) into your product, authenticated with HTTP Basic auth.
